    Epidemiology

    Epidemiology systems of infection and recovery.

    The systems are compartmental, network, metapopulation, and agent-based.

    ActiveHostElement(label, visual=None, *, i=0.0, a=0.1, lam=0.3, mu=0.1)

    Bases: Element

    Node of an activity-driven network, susceptible or infected, in discrete time.

    The node is susceptible at i = 0 and infected at i = 1.

    A TransitionInteraction recovers an infected node with probability mu in a step, and another infects a susceptible node with probability lam by every infected neighbour along the edges of the previous step. A TopologyInteraction joins the node to other nodes with the probability a, its activity.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The label of the node or of the group of nodes.

    		 required
    visual VisualSpec | None

    How the element is drawn, or None for default_visual_.

    		 None
    i Annotated[float, StateSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    Whether the node is infected.

    		 0.0
    a Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The activity, the probability of firing at a step.

    		 0.1
    lam Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The probability of infection along one edge.

    		 0.3
    mu Annotated[float, ParameterSpec(domain=closed_open(0, oo))]

    The probability of recovery at a step.

    		 0.1

    Examples:

    >>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.epidemiology import ActiveHostElement
>>> ActiveHostElement('node').mu
0.1

    ActivityDrivenEpidemicsSystem(n=500, *, m=2, exponent=2.2, least=0.01, lam=0.9, mu=0.1, infected=0.05, seed=1, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    SIS spreading on an activity-driven temporal network, whose edges last one step.

    At every step every node fires with probability its activity, drawn from a^-exponent above least, and joins m random nodes. The infection travels along the edges of a step, which disappear at the next step, so it spreads only when lam / mu exceeds a threshold set by the moments of the activity, 2 <a> / (m (<a> + sqrt(<a^2>))) in the limit of small probabilities, and not by the degrees of the network aggregated over time. The system has the states hosts.i and activities hosts.a of the group hosts on the nodes, and the variable group contacts on the edges of every step.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    n int

    The number of nodes.

    		 500
    m int

    The number of edges an active node creates.

    		 2
    exponent float

    The exponent of the power-law distribution of activities.

    		 2.2
    least float

    The smallest activity.

    		 0.01
    lam float

    The probability of infection along one edge.

    		 0.9
    mu float

    The probability of recovery at a step.

    		 0.1
    infected float

    The initial share of infected nodes.

    		 0.05
    seed int | None

    The seed of the activities and the initial infections.

    		 1
    label str

    The label of the system, which names it when it is nested in another one.

    		 'system'

    AdaptiveSISSystem(n=200, k=6.0, *, beta=0.4, gamma=1.0, w=1.0, infected=0.2, seed=1, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    The SIS epidemic where susceptible nodes cut their edges to infected neighbours.

    Every edge between a susceptible and an infected node is rewired at rate w: the susceptible end keeps it and joins it to another susceptible node. Rewiring isolates the infected nodes and raises the epidemic threshold above its value on the fixed network, while the susceptible nodes cluster. The system has the states hosts.i of the variable group hosts on the nodes and the variable group contacts on the edges.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    n int

    The number of nodes.

    		 200
    k float

    The mean degree of the initial Erdős-Rényi network.

    		 6.0
    beta float

    The infection rate per edge to an infected neighbour.

    		 0.4
    gamma float

    The recovery rate.

    		 1.0
    w float

    The rewiring rate of an edge between a susceptible and an infected node.

    		 1.0
    infected float

    The initial share of infected nodes.

    		 0.2
    seed int | None

    The seed of the network and of the initial infections.

    		 1
    label str

    The label of the system, which names it when it is nested in another one.

    		 'system'

    Examples:

    >>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.epidemiology import AdaptiveSISSystem
>>> [component.label for component in AdaptiveSISSystem(n=20).prepare().system_.elements]

    AgentBasedSIRSystem(width=50, height=50, *, people=500, infected=5, d=0.8, beta=0.6, gamma=0.02, mu=0.0, alpha=0.0, incubation=0.0, lockdown_start=0.0, lockdown_length=0.0, lockdown_d=0.1, random_state=0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    People who walk on a grid and infect those in their cell.

    The basic system infects with probability beta and recovers with probability gamma. Its final size depends on beta and gamma separately, not only on their ratio, because walking limits the contacts. Mortality mu, waning immunity alpha, an incubation of incubation steps, and a lockdown that lowers the probability of moving to lockdown_d extend it. The system has the group people.

    ColocationInteraction(label, *, people, p=0.05, gamma=0.1, closed=False)

    Bases: Interaction

    Daily movement of people between home and work, and infection at locations.

    A step is half a day: in even steps every person is at home and in odd steps at the workplace, unless workplaces are closed, the time-labelled visits of the bipartite graph of people and locations of EpiSims. At every step a susceptible person is infected with the probability 1 - (1 - p)^k by the k infected people at the same location, and an infected person recovers with the probability gamma.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The label of the interaction.

    people Annotated[str, RoleSpec()]

    		 required
    p float

    The probability of transmission per infected contact and step.

    		 0.05
    gamma float

    The probability of recovery per step.

    		 0.1
    closed bool

    Whether the workplaces are closed, so people stay at home.

    		 False

    Examples:

    def visit(self, system: SystemView) -> None:
    """Move every person to the location of the half day, then infect and recover.

    Args:
        system:
            The system.
    """
    people = system.get_agents(self.people, CommuterView)
    at_work = round(system.time) % 2 == 1 and not self.closed
    places = np.array([int(person.work if at_work else person.home) for person in people])
    health = np.array([person.health for person in people])
    infected = np.bincount(places[health == INFECTED], minlength=places.max() + 1)[places]
    draws = system.rng.random(len(people))
    infection = (health == SUSCEPTIBLE) & (draws < 1 - (1 - self.p) ** infected)
    recovery = (health == INFECTED) & (draws < self.gamma)
    health = np.where(infection, INFECTED, np.where(recovery, RECOVERED, health))
    for person, place, state in zip(people, places, health, strict=True):
        person.move_to(int(place))
        person.health = float(state)

    CovidTransmissionInteraction(label, *, target, contacts, temperature=0.1, hard=False)

    Bases: Interaction

    Infection and recovery of agents by relaxed Bernoulli draws, Eq. 6 of Quera-Bofarull et al. (2023).

    A susceptible agent is infected with the probability 1 - exp(-psi sum_L beta_L I_L), where I_L is the share of infected agents among the other members of its place of kind L, household, school, or company, read through a weighted sum with the weights 1 / (n_L - 1) of co-members. An infected agent recovers with the probability gamma. Both are Bernoulli draws with a temperature, which every backend but JAX draws exactly, and JAX relaxes so runs have gradients in the transmissions. The interaction declares its draws reparameterized.

    label str

    The label of the interaction.

    The weights of the co-members of every agent at its places, one matrix per kind of place.

    		 required
    temperature float

    The temperature of the relaxed draws on JAX.

    		 0.1
    hard bool

    Whether JAX runs draw exact agents with the gradients of the relaxation.

    		 False

    DegreeClassElement(label, visual=None, *, rho=0.01, lam=0.2, k=1.0, P=1.0)

    Bases: Element

    Infected density of the nodes of one degree, in heterogeneous mean field.

    A node of degree k recovers at rate 1 and is infected at rate lam k Theta, where Theta = sum_k k P(k) rho_k / <k> is the probability that an edge points to an infected node, a total over the degree classes, so d rho_k / dt = -rho_k + lam k (1 - rho_k) Theta. The classes are the members of a group, and the recovery and the infection are interactions of the group, which HeterogeneousMeanFieldSISSystem adds.

    DelayedSIRSSystem(first=0.01, second=0.0, *, a=2.0, recovery=6, e=0.005, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    Two cities with recurrent outbreaks of a disease.

    The disease has fixed infection and immunity periods.

    With one infected step and recovery immune steps, each city follows x' = a x (1 - x - x(t-1) - ... - x(t-recovery)), which reduces to the logistic map without immunity. Outbreaks recur like relaxation oscillations, and the visits of a fraction e of the infected couple the two cities, whose outbreaks lock in or out of phase. The system has the centers first and second.

    Differentiable agents of a COVID-19 epidemic, after Quera-Bofarull et al. (2023).

    The model of Quera-Bofarull et al. (2023, arXiv 2305.15340), a small version of GradABM-JUNE: a seeded synthetic population of households of two adults and two children, where children go to schools and adults to companies. Agents are susceptible, infected, or recovered, and are infected and recover by the relaxed Bernoulli draws of CovidTransmissionInteraction, Eq. 6, with a transmission beta_L per kind of place. NumPy runs draw exact agents and JAX runs relax the draws, so the system holds the tag differentiable and variational calibration fits the three transmissions through its JAX run. Time runs in days. The system has the group people, the element cases with the infections of children and adults of the day before, and the observable daily_infections.

    EpisimsCitySystem(people=1000, *, household=3.0, workplace=20.0, p=0.05, gamma=0.1, infected=5, closed=False, seed=0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    A synthetic city in the spirit of EpiSims.

    People infect those they meet at home and at work.

    EpiSims models a city as a bipartite graph of people and locations whose edges are visits labelled with their times, and spreads disease between people at the same location. Here every person belongs to a household of mean size household and a workplace or school of mean size workplace, the people sleep at home and work by day, and the disease spreads by SIR contacts at every location. The locations form a network whose edges join a home to the workplaces of its members, the projection of the bipartite graph onto the locations. Households spread the disease within families and workplaces between them, so closing the workplaces, one of the interventions EpiSims was built to compare, confines outbreaks to households. The system has the homes, workplaces, and health states of the agent group people on the locations.

    HeterogeneousMeanFieldSIRSystem(exponent=2.5, k_min=3, k_max=100, *, beta=0.1, mu=1.0, infected=0.0001, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    The SIR epidemic on an uncorrelated network of power-law degrees.

    It is in heterogeneous mean field.

    The degrees run from k_min to k_max with P(k) ~ k^-exponent. An outbreak grows when beta / mu > <k> / (<k^2> - <k>), a threshold close to <k> / <k^2> on heterogeneous networks, which vanishes on scale-free networks as k_max grows. Below it the epidemic dies out after infecting a share of the order of the initial one, and above it a finite share of the population ends recovered. The hubs are infected first. The system has the densities network.s, network.i, and network.r of the degree classes from k_min to k_max, members of the group network, and the shares infected and recovered of the whole population, the last one the final epidemic size at the end of the outbreak.

    ImmunizingDegreeClassElement(label, visual=None, *, s=0.999, i=0.001, r=0.0, beta=0.1, mu=1.0, k=1.0, P=1.0)

    Bases: Element

    Susceptible, infected, and recovered densities of the nodes of one degree.

    The densities are in heterogeneous mean field.

    A susceptible node of degree k is infected at rate beta k theta and an infected node recovers at rate mu, so d i_k / dt = -mu i_k + beta k s_k theta and d r_k / dt = mu i_k. On an uncorrelated network, the probability that a contact of a susceptible node is infected is theta = sum_k (k - 1) P(k) i_k / <k>, a total over the degree classes, since an infected neighbour of degree k has at most k - 1 other contacts. The classes are the members of a group, and the infections and the recoveries are interactions of the group, which HeterogeneousMeanFieldSIRSystem adds.

    PairFormationSISSystem(n=400, k=2, *, beta=None, gamma=0.5, sigma=None, pressure=1.5, turnover=2.0, infected=0.05, seed=1, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    The SIS epidemic on partnerships that dissolve and are replaced at once.

    Every person keeps k partners at any time, on a random regular network. A partnership dissolves at the rate sigma, and the person who keeps it finds a new partner at once, at random. An infectious person infects a susceptible partner at the rate beta and recovers at the rate gamma. By default the infection pressure k beta and the rate k sigma of new partners per person are held fixed at pressure and turnover, so k = 1 is serial monogamy and a larger k is concurrency at the same contact rate. Concurrency lets the infection pass on before the partnership that brought it ends, so the epidemic grows faster and reaches more people. The system has the states people.i of the variable group people on the nodes and the variable group partnerships on the edges.

    PartnershipEpidemicElement(label, visual=None, *, S=0.99, E=0.0, I=0.01, R=0.0, J=0.0, c=2.0, beta=0.2, tau=1.0, T=0.5, nu=0.1)

    Bases: Element

    Population of Watts and May whose infections pass along lasting partnerships.

    The population has a fixed exposed period.

    Susceptible people S acquire new partners at the rate c, each infecting with the probability beta over the partnership, and are infected at the rate pi = c beta (I / A + J) with the active population A = S + E + I. The first term is the infection by a new partner who is infectious, and the memory J is the infection by a current partner who turned infectious after the partnership formed, dJ/dt = pi(t - T) S(t - T) / A - J / tau, where partnerships last a mean time tau. The exposed E turn infectious after the fixed time T, and the infectious I develop the disease, which ends their sexual activity, at the rate nu, into R. The infection starts at time zero, so the infectious and the memory are zero before it.

    PersonElement(label, visual=VisualSpec('agents', {'color_by': 'health', 'color_range': (0.0, 4.0)}), *, health=SUSCEPTIBLE, d=0.8, beta=0.6, gamma=0.01, mu=0.0, alpha=0.0, lockdown_start=0.0, lockdown_length=0.0, lockdown_d=0.1)

    Bases: Element

    Person of the agent-based SIR system.

    The person has incubation, mortality, waning immunity, and lockdown.

    A MovementInteraction walks a living person to a neighbouring cell with probability d, or lockdown_d during the lockdown, which lasts lockdown_length steps from lockdown_start. Transitions of the agent form, which AgentBasedSIRSystem adds, move the health of the person. An infectious person infects, with probability beta, every susceptible person in its cell, who becomes exposed. An infectious person recovers with probability gamma or dies with probability mu, and a recovered person loses immunity with probability alpha. Health is 0 susceptible, 1 exposed, 2 infected, 3 recovered, or 4 dead.

    The incubation follows the convention of the residence time after of TransitionInteraction: the step of the exposure counts as the first step in the exposed state, so a person exposed in step n becomes infectious at the end of step n + incubation - 1. The clock that the person kept before counted the step of the exposure only when the person acted after its infector in that step, so the onset now comes half a step earlier on average.

    label str

    Bases: BaseSystem

    Random walkers among whom one sick walker starts a deadly epidemic.

    The walkers move on a grid or on a network.

    Sick walkers infect the walkers they meet in a cell and die lifetime steps later, so the epidemic spreads as a front like a forest fire and burns out. Above a critical density of walkers it percolates across the grid. On a network, such as a small world of cities, walkers travel along edges and long links carry the disease far. The system has the group walkers.

    RecordDynamicsEpidemicSystem(n=10000, *, seed=0, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    Yearly strains that infect every resident less resistant than their strength.

    The infected residents become immune.

    Every resident keeps a resistance R drawn uniformly from [0, 1]. Once a year a strain of strength eta, drawn uniformly from [0, 1), infects the residents with R < eta, whose resistance becomes 1. In a large population an outbreak happens only in a year whose strain is stronger than every earlier one, a record, so outbreaks thin out as time goes on: the mean number of outbreaks in t years is close to the harmonic number H_t, about ln t + 0.577, a Poisson process in the logarithm of time. The system has the resistances residents.R, the infections of the last year residents.infected, and the strength pathogen.eta of the strain of the coming year.

    SpreadingInteraction(label, *, target, state='state', beta=1.0, gamma=0.0, omega=0.0, inactive=0.0, active=1.0, removed=None, form='number', layer=None)

    Bases: TransitionInteraction

    Spreading of the active value of a discrete state to neighbours.

    The neighbours are along the edges of a network or the bonds of a lattice.

    An inactive member becomes active at the rate beta times the number of its active neighbours, or times their fraction of its neighbours. An active member recovers at the rate gamma, to the inactive value, or to the removed value when there is one, and a removed member returns to the inactive value at the rate omega. Every move is a transition at a rate, so the state changes by random events in continuous time.

    WattsMayConcurrencySystem(infected=0.01, *, c=2.0, beta=0.2, tau=1.0, T=0.5, nu=0.1, label='system')

    Bases: BaseSystem

    The SEIR epidemic of Watts and May.

    Partnerships that last longer spread the infection faster.

    A susceptible person is infected at the rate pi(t) = c beta [I / (S + E + I) + int exp(-(t - t') / tau) pi(t' - T) S(t' - T) / (S + E + I)(t') dt'], by a new partner who is infectious or by a current partner who turned infectious during the partnership. The mean number of current partners is c tau, so a longer partnership raises the mean degree of the momentary network, and the infection rate grows with tau at fixed c and beta. The system has the fractions population.S, population.E, population.I, population.R, and the infection memory population.J.

    ZombieOutbreakSystem(susceptible=500.0, zombies=1.0, removed=0.0, *, birth=0.0, beta=0.0095, alpha=0.005, delta=0.0001, zeta=0.0001, stochastic=False, label='system')

    Bases: ReactionNetworkSystem

    The outbreak of zombies of Munz et al.

    The dead rise again and humans are eventually overrun.

    Humans S are born at the rate birth and die naturally at the rate delta. A zombie Z bites a human at the rate beta S Z, and humans destroy zombies at the rate alpha S Z. The dead and destroyed R rise as zombies at the rate zeta. Without births the total S + Z + R is conserved, and with resurrection the only stable state is the doomsday state without humans, whatever the initial numbers, whenever beta > alpha. The system has the compartments S, Z, and R.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    susceptible float

    The initial number of humans.

    		 500.0
    zombies float

    The initial number of zombies.

    		 1.0
    removed float

    The initial number of dead and destroyed.

    		 0.0
    birth float

    The birth rate of humans.

    		 0.0
    beta float

    The rate at which zombies turn humans.

    		 0.0095
    alpha float

    The rate at which humans destroy zombies.

    		 0.005
    delta float

    The rate of natural death of humans.

    		 0.0001
    zeta float

    The rate at which the removed rise as zombies.

    		 0.0001
    stochastic bool

    Whether every event moves one individual at random times.

    		 False
    label str

    The label of the system, which names it when it is nested in another one.

    		 'system'

    Examples:

    >>> from skcomplex.systems.biology.epidemiology import ZombieOutbreakSystem
>>> [element.label for element in ZombieOutbreakSystem().prepare().system_.elements]
['S', 'Z', 'R']

    def __init__(
    self,
    susceptible: float = 500.0,
    zombies: float = 1.0,
    removed: float = 0.0,
    *,
    birth: float = 0.0,
    beta: float = 0.0095,
    alpha: float = 0.005,
    delta: float = 0.0001,
    zeta: float = 0.0001,
    stochastic: bool = False,
    label: str = 'system',
) -> None:
    super().__init__(label=label)
    self.susceptible = susceptible
    self.zombies = zombies
    self.removed = removed
    self.birth = birth
    self.beta = beta
    self.alpha = alpha
    self.delta = delta
    self.zeta = zeta
    self.stochastic = stochastic
